title: Protocol for ex vivo physicochemical assessment of photothermally preconditioned platelet-rich plasma
author: Cordero, Sánchez-Vizcaíno Mengual, et al.
materials: In the validation dataset, pH was measured with a Jenway pH550 portable pH meter (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). The pH 7.0 and pH 10.0 calibration buffers were selected according to the manufacturer’s instructions because the expected pH range of citrate-anticoagulated PRP was near-neutral to slightly alkaline.

Sample temperature is recorded at the same predefined time points used for density/turbidity and pH. Temperature was measured simultaneously with pH using a Jenway pH550 portable pH meter (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA).

steps.title: Collect donor blood
steps.instruction: Recruit healthy adult donors (age ≥ 18 y, no acute infection, no visible haemolysis or clotting) who have provided written informed consent; draw a total of 64 mL peripheral whole blood per donor into eight Vacutainer tubes each pre‑filled with 9 mL of 3.8 % sodium citrate (Sanisus Medical, Castellón, Spain); gently invert tubes according to the manufacturer’s instructions, avoiding vigorous shaking.

steps.title: Prepare PRP by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the citrate‑anticoagulated tubes at 1800 rpm for 8 min at room temperature; carefully collect the platelet‑rich plasma fraction (~2 mL per tube, ≈16 mL total per donor) and transfer all fractions into a sterile 20 mL tube, mixing gently to obtain a homogeneous donor‑specific pooled PRP sample.

steps.title: Allocate paired PRP aliquots
steps.instruction: Divide the pooled PRP into two equal aliquots of ≈8 mL each; label one as “Control” (standard PRP) and the other as “Treated” (PTBM‑PRP); transfer each aliquot into a separate sterile 15 mL tube and keep the paired tubes together for parallel processing.

steps.title: Apply photothermal biomodulation
steps.instruction: Place the 8 mL Treated aliquot into the sterile single‑use PTBM kit compatible with the Meta Cell Technology MCT System; run the PTBM‑PRP preset: 620 nm wavelength, 1 J/cm² fluence, sample temperature set to 4 °C, exposure time 15 min, using the ≈8 mL sample volume; keep the Control aliquot under identical laboratory conditions but without PTBM exposure.

steps.title: Set measurement schedule
steps.instruction: Perform measurements at the following time points for both aliquots: t = 0 min (baseline, before PTBM), t = 15 min (immediately after PTBM), then every 5 min thereafter (t = 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60 min).

steps.title: Measure density/turbidity
steps.instruction: Switch on the DEN‑1 McFarland densitometer (Biosan, Novosibirsk, Russia) ≈45 min before the first measurement to allow stabilization; for each time point, transfer a minimum of 2 mL PRP into a standardized 16‑mm glass tube, insert the tube into the densitometer, record the McFarland value, and note donor code, sample condition, time point, operator initials, and any visible abnormality (clotting, haemolysis, sedimentation, air bubbles). Use the same tube type for all readings.

steps.title: Measure pH
steps.instruction: Prepare the Jenway pH550 portable pH meter (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) ≈90 min before use; hydrate the microelectrode, perform a two‑point calibration with pH 7.0 and pH 10.0 buffers, confirm acceptable calibration, then for each time point use a minimum of 5 mL PRP, insert the electrode, allow the reading to stabilize, record the pH value, rinse the electrode with distilled water before the next sample, and store the electrode in pH 7.0 buffer when not in use; after all measurements soak the electrode in a protein‑cleaning solution for 15–30 min. Record donor code, sample condition, time point, pH value, calibration buffers used, calibration status, operator initials, and any technical issues.

steps.title: Measure temperature
steps.instruction: Using a calibrated temperature probe (or the temperature sensor of the Jenway pH550), measure the temperature of each aliquot at every predefined time point (baseline, immediately post‑PTBM, and every 5 min to 60 min); record temperature in °C, donor code, sample condition, time point, ambient laboratory temperature if available, and operator initials.

steps.title: Perform quality‑control checks
steps.instruction: Throughout the workflow, ensure: same anticoagulant type and tube format for all donors; identical centrifugation parameters; pooling before aliquot allocation; paired control and treated aliquots from the same donor; identical measurement schedule; pH meter calibrated before use; densitometer stabilized before use; same tube type for density/turbidity; and documentation of any protocol deviations.

steps.title: Record and analyse data
steps.instruction: For each donor and each condition, compile density/turbidity, pH, and temperature values at all time points; summarize data as individual donor values, mean ± standard deviation, paired differences between standard and PTBM‑PRP, and generate time‑course plots; perform descriptive comparisons of baseline versus post‑preconditioning values, noting that statistical testing should be interpreted cautiously for small pilot datasets.
